title: Recording March of the Bobcat with Albert Elkhorn
summary: Gorman and the interviewer recall recording numbers together with a young man from Switzerland, and never hearing from him afterward.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Crossed the river there one time.
That's right, me and Albert Elkhorn, I cut the March of the Bobcat for you all, didn't
it? I don't remember what pieces now anymore.
Yeah, March of the Bobcat, and I believe this was High Society. You remember the boy from Switzerland, eh?
Yes. I never heard from this boy.
I never did either. I don't know what happened to him.
I believe we played four numbers there. We caught, let me see, the Muscat Ramble, the March of the Bobcat, and it was High Society. It was other numbers, you remember?
Yeah, I think you was in New York at that time. We had just come down, eh?
Yes, Pittsburgh and New York, up in there someplace. I stayed in both towns, part of the way.

Well, I talk, but I studied many times. I said, well, I said, he was telling me, he said, well, he's going and then he's going to write me and tell me just how it made out, but I never did got no, no letter from this dollar.
